memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'This is to have the force of law for you throughout the generations to come, wherever you live. Anyone who kills a person is to be put to death as a murderer only on the testimony of witnesses. But no one is to be put to death on the testimony of only one witness. Do not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer, who deserves to die. They are to be put to death.'" - Num 35:29-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God builds safeguards into His justice. No one could be put to death on the word of a single witness; multiple witnesses were required to establish the truth. This protected against false accusation and hasty condemnation. God's justice was to be careful, thorough, and based on established truth, not on rumour or the testimony of one possibly biased or mistaken voice.

This reflects God's deep commitment to truth and fairness. Human justice can be corrupted by lies, by a single false accuser, by the rush to condemn. God guarded against this by requiring corroboration. He wanted His people to be a community where truth was established carefully and where the innocent were protected from false charges. This principle carried into the New Testament church as well (2 Cor 13:1; 1 Tim 5:19).

There is a lesson here for how we handle accusations and reports about others. We should not be quick to believe or spread a single, unverified claim. We should seek the truth, listen to more than one side, and refuse to condemn on rumour. This is part of loving our neighbour and reflecting God's own justice.

We can also take comfort in this: our God does not judge us on false testimony or the accusations of the enemy. Satan is called the accuser of God's people (Rev 12:10), but his accusations cannot stand against those covered by Christ. When the enemy accuses us, we have an Advocate — Jesus Christ, the Righteous One — who speaks in our defence (1 John 2:1). In Him, the case against us is answered by His own blood. The God of true justice has justified us in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you careful to seek the truth before believing accusations about others?
2. How does God's commitment to true justice shape your own dealings?
3. What comfort do you find in Christ answering every accusation against you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: God of truth and justice, help me to seek the truth carefully and never to condemn on rumour. Thank You that in Christ, my Advocate, every accusation against me is answered by His blood. Amen.
